channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Criminal Liability for Stalking from September 2025
item.description: Kazakhstan introduced criminal liability for stalking on September 16, 2025. As of June 9, 2026, 83 criminal cases related to stalking have been sent to court. Almaty registered 24 applications concerning stalking from early 2026 to the end of April.

item.title: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Claims Over 5,000 Lives, WHO Reports
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in 5,026 confirmed deaths and 10,351 infections. Currently, 1,101 individuals are undergoing treatment or quarantine, while 2,788 have recovered. Experts suggest the actual death toll may be higher due to undetected spread.

item.title: WHO Warns of Global Spread of New 'Ultramutant' Coronavirus Variant PJ.2.1
item.description: The World Health Organization warns of increased risks from the new coronavirus variant PJ.2.1, an 'ultramutant' first detected in Canada in May 2026. While it has many mutations, there's no confirmation it causes more severe illness. It is actively circulating in the US, Canada, and Europe.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains 125 Violators and 44 Vessels in Caspian Sea During October
item.description: Kazakhstan's border guards detained 126 offenders and 44 small vessels in the Caspian Sea during October. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 11.5 kg of narcotics and 88 km of illegal fishing gear. Over 2,300 fish were released back into their natural habitat, and fines totaling over 4.5 million tenge were imposed.

item.title: Fake Diploma Costs Kyrgyz Citizen Russian Citizenship Opportunity
item.description: A citizen of Kyrgyzstan has lost her status as a participant in Russia's state program for voluntary resettlement due to a fake diploma. Russian authorities discovered she submitted fraudulent documents to prove qualifications and language proficiency, leading to the annulment of her program status and denial of citizenship.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Diplomatic Relations with All UN Member States
item.description: Kazakhstan has established diplomatic relations with Nauru, its 195th UN member state. This marks the completion of Kazakhstan's process of establishing diplomatic ties with all UN member nations, a significant milestone for its diplomacy. Discussions focused on political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Growth Approaches Uzbekistan's, Outpacing in Average Wages
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is emerging as a regional economic leader, with its GDP growing nearly 50% in five years under President Japarov. The country is undertaking major infrastructure projects and is now catching up to Uzbekistan in some economic indicators, having already surpassed it in average wages.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Allocate 6.5 Trillion Tenge from National Fund for Infrastructure
item.description: Kazakhstan plans an unprecedented infrastructure modernization, allocating approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by the end of 2029. President Tokayev proposed naming this initiative 'People's Construction'. The funds will be used for social, transport, and engineering facilities nationwide.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish State Commission to Oversee 'People's Construction' Program
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced the creation of a state commission to strictly monitor the spending of budget funds during the implementation of the 'People's Construction' program. The commission will include government officials, parliament members, and public figures.

item.title: Police Arrest Man in Shymkent for Alleged Housing Scam in Astana
item.description: Police in Astana have arrested a 45-year-old man in Shymkent who was internationally wanted for an alleged housing scam. The suspect, along with accomplices, allegedly defrauded citizens by attracting funds for an apartment complex construction without proper permits or state expert review. Over 292 investors were affected, with total damages exceeding 4 billion tenge.

item.title: WHO Director-General Praises Kazakhstan's Commitment to "Health for All"
item.description: The Director-General of the World Health Organization, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, has highly praised Kazakhstan's attention to public health and well-being. He highlighted President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's commitment to increasing the salaries of 77,000 healthcare workers and investing in primary healthcare. Ghebreyesus noted Kazakhstan's role in the 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration and its continued practical implementation of its principles.

item.title: EU and Canada Launch New Partnership Alliance for Future Prosperity
item.description: The European Union and Canada have launched a new partnership format, the "EU-Canada Alliance for the Future," aimed at creating a common space for prosperity and economic security. The alliance will focus on mutual reciprocity in industrial sectors, deeper strategic cooperation, and building more integrated supply chains. It also includes enhanced cooperation in foreign policy, security, crisis management, and addressing hybrid threats.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Secures Silver Medal at World Equestrian Tourism Championship
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has won a silver medal at the first-ever World Championship for Equestrian Tourism, held in Cholpon-Ata on the shores of Issyk-Kul Lake. Teams from Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Germany participated. Athletes demonstrated riding skills, endurance, tactical preparation, and navigation abilities. Russia took first place, and Kazakhstan secured third.

item.title: Taliban Claim Pakistan Unwilling to Pursue Peaceful Resolution of Tensions
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid stated that the group has made efforts for a peaceful resolution of tensions with Pakistan, but these have been unsuccessful. He asserted that Pakistan is unwilling to adopt a peaceful approach. Mujahid claimed the Taliban are in a defensive position and not the initiators of the conflict, which stems from Pakistan's concerns over militant groups operating from Afghan soil.

item.title: WHO Praises Kazakhstan's Plan to Increase Healthcare Worker Salaries
item.description: The World Health Organization has endorsed Kazakhstan's initiative to raise salaries for 77,000 healthcare professionals. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus expressed support for President Tokayev's commitment to investing in primary healthcare and prioritizing public well-being. This move aligns with the global 'Health for All' vision, a principle established by the 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Announces Creation of State Commission for 'People's Construction' Oversight
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has announced the establishment of a state commission tasked with overseeing the 'People's Construction' project. This initiative aims to ensure proper management and accountability for the development project, though further details on the commission's specific mandate were not immediately provided.

item.title: Uzbekistan Implements Dual Education to Meet Labor Market Demands
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its vocational education system by integrating dual education. This approach aims to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, ensuring graduates are better prepared for real-world job requirements and improving youth employment rates.

item.title: Uzbekistan Improves Position in International Rule of Law Index
item.description: Uzbekistan has seen a stable increase in its standing in several international rankings, including the Rule of Law Index. The World Justice Project's index assesses legal systems across 143 countries, with Uzbekistan showing positive movement in this critical area.

item.title: WHO Head Praises Kazakhstan's Healthcare Support Policies
item.description: World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus commended Kazakhstan's work on health and public well-being. He highlighted President Tokayev's initiative to raise salaries for 77,000 medical workers, noting it improves service quality and accessibility.

item.title: Russia Tightens Measures Against Migrants Violating Laws from November 3
item.description: Starting November 3, Russia will implement stricter measures against migrants who violate the country's laws. The State Duma has expanded the list of offenses punishable by expulsion, doubling the number of relevant administrative code articles from 22 to 45. Violations include disobedience to police, spreading offensive content online, and discrimination.

item.title: UN Warns of Civilian Risk Amid Renewed Clashes Near Torkham Border
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has warned that renewed clashes near the Torkham border crossing are endangering civilians and humanitarian workers. A child was killed and a worker injured in recent fighting. The ongoing conflict threatens local communities and complicates the return of Afghans from Pakistan.

item.title: Polish President Returns Amidst 'Coup' Dispute, Constitutional Court Head Removed
item.description: Poland's President has cut short a foreign trip due to a political dispute, described by some as a 'coup'. The head of the Constitutional Tribunal was dismissed, and the building was surrounded by police. The Prime Minister frames it as restoring law, while the opposition calls it a coup.

item.title: Azerbaijan's President Absent from Organization of Turkic States Summit
item.description: The President of Azerbaijan was notably absent from the recent summit of the Organization of Turkic States. The reasons for his non-attendance were not immediately clear, raising questions about regional dynamics.

item.title: CIS Customs Chiefs Meet in Dushanbe to Discuss Combating Smuggling
item.description: The 26th meeting of heads of law enforcement units of the CIS Customs Services Council convened in Dushanbe on October 30, 2026. The meeting, timed to coincide with the CIS's 35th anniversary, focused on strengthening coordination to combat transnational crime, drug trafficking, and customs violations. Representatives from eight CIS member states attended.

item.title: Kazakh Farmers Increasingly Taking Out Loans in Foreign Currency
item.description: Kazakh farmers are increasingly taking out loans in foreign currency, according to LS. As of October 1, banks had issued 645.7 billion tenge in agricultural loans, a 7.4% increase since the start of the year. While tenge loans dominate, foreign currency loans grew significantly, reaching 13.4 billion tenge. Almaty and Astana lead in loan volume.

item.title: Kazakhstan's New Constitution Establishes Single-Chamber Kurultai for Legislative Power
item.description: Kazakhstan's new constitution introduces significant changes to the state governance system, redefining inter-branch relations. The establishment of a single-chamber Kurultai is a key step in modernizing the political system. This body is now tasked not only with adopting laws but also ensuring the implementation of constitutional principles.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Man Arrested After Wife Complained to President About Bigamy
item.description: A man in Kyrgyzstan has been arrested and detained until November 20 following a complaint filed by his wife with President Sadyr Japarov. The wife accused her husband of bigamy and attempting to dispossess her and their three children. The president had urged law enforcement to ensure justice in such cases.

item.title: Astana Housing Fraud Suspect Arrested After Stealing 4 Billion Tenge
item.description: Police in Shymkent have arrested a 45-year-old man wanted internationally for large-scale construction fraud. The suspect and accomplices allegedly took money from 292 investors for an illegal housing project in Astana, causing over 4 billion tenge in damages. He was apprehended after evading capture by frequently changing residences.

item.title: Ebola Death Toll in DR Congo Surpasses 5,000
item.description: The death toll from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has exceeded 5,000, with over 10,000 infections reported since the outbreak began in May. Authorities are struggling to contain the epidemic, which has spread to eight provinces, exacerbated by delayed diagnosis and conflict.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New Ambassadors to Morocco and Cuba
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has made changes in the diplomatic corps, appointing Ainur Danenova as Ambassador to the Kingdom of Morocco. Olzhas Issabekov will represent the country in Cuba, replacing Andriyan Yelemesov, who has been relieved of his post.

item.title: UNHCR Reports 6.3 Million Afghans Returned Since 2023, Many Under Duress
item.description: The UNHCR reports that approximately 6.3 million Afghans have returned since 2023, with about 60 percent allegedly forced. UNHCR representative Arafat Jamal cited poverty, unemployment, and reduced aid as worsening conditions. Returnees face challenges in Afghanistan, with many selling possessions to fund their travel.

item.title: Ship Attacks in Strait of Hormuz Hit Record High in October
item.description: UKMTO data reveals a record number of ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz during October, with at least 35 incidents reported in the Persian Gulf and strait. This marks the worst month since the US-Iran conflict began. Iran's IRGC claimed four vessels caught fire after striking naval mines.

item.title: Afghan Envoy Highlights Migrant Deportation Concerns at IOM Meeting
item.description: Afghanistan's ambassador to Switzerland, Nasir Ahmad Andisha, raised concerns about forced deportations and challenges facing returnees at an International Organization for Migration (IOM) meeting. The IOM's budget prioritizes Afghanistan, and Taliban restrictions on women hinder economic recovery and migrant reintegration, the meeting noted.

item.title: Over 120 Violators Detained in Caspian Sea Special Operations
item.description: Special operations in the Caspian Sea have resulted in the detention of 126 violators and 44 small vessels. Authorities seized 11.5 kg of narcotics and 88 kilometers of poaching gear. The National Security Committee reported that fines exceeded 4.5 million tenge, with prevented damages estimated at over 840 million tenge.

item.title: Tajikistan's Water Share from Amu Darya and Syr Darya Determined for Autumn and Winter
item.description: Tajikistan's share of water usage from the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers for the six months of autumn and winter has been determined. The article poses a question about the exact share of Tajikistan from these rivers.

item.title: Turkic World's Common Information Space: From Cooperation to Concrete Projects
item.description: The 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States, themed 'Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Action,' was held in Ankara. The Turkic World Dialogue Forum focused on developing information and media cooperation among member states. The 'Future of the Turkic World 2040' document outlines long-term cooperation goals.

item.title: Former President Nazarbayev's Relative's Luxury Almaty Hotel Sold at Auction
item.description: A luxury hotel in Almaty, previously owned by Kairat Satybaldy, a relative of former President Nursultan Nazarbayev, has been sold at auction. The DoubleTree by Hilton hotel was sold for approximately $27.5 million after three previous attempts. Satybaldy was previously imprisoned for embezzlement.

item.title: Tajikistan Approves Civil Aviation Security Program Until 2030
item.description: The government of Tajikistan has approved the National Civil Aviation Security Program for 2026-2030. The program aims to enhance passenger and aircraft safety, protect citizens' lives and health, and fulfill international obligations. It includes expanding air travel, modernizing infrastructure, and countering modern threats like cyber threats.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New Ambassadors to Morocco and Cuba
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Ainur Danenova and Olzhas Issabekov as Kazakhstan's new ambassadors to Morocco and Cuba, respectively. The Akorda announced the personnel changes. Danenova will serve as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to the Kingdom of Morocco, while Issabekov takes on the same role in the Republic of Cuba.

item.title: Man Dies After Self-Immolation Outside Court in Semey, Kazakhstan
item.description: A man has reportedly died after setting himself on fire outside the court building in Semey, Kazakhstan. The incident occurred on October 30th. Police have opened a criminal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the event. The identity and age of the deceased have not yet been released.
